MEMBER.NAME: adapter_name_raw
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Created by retype action

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_fw_raw
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Created by retype action

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x00
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown. Checked in state transitions (exact role TBD).

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x01
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown.

MEMBER.NAME: source_mac
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Console Ethernet MAC (6 bytes). Written to XPP_EthFrame.src_mac on every outbound frame. Source: set during wlan_network_object construction from NIC adapter.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x08
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown (4 bytes).

MEMBER.NAME: request_state
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Pending request type byte: 0 = idle 1 = HANDSHAKE in flight 2 = NETWORKS_LIST in flight 3 = ADAPTER_INFO in flight 4 = CONNECT in flight 5 = BEACON/scan in flight Cleared to 0 on response receipt or timeout.

MEMBER.NAME: is_connected
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 1 = adapter authenticated and connected to a network. Set by my_handle_nlb_handshake_response on success. Read by xpp_rssi_is_connected guard (this+0x0d == 0x01).

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x0e
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown (6 bytes).

MEMBER.NAME: nlb_frame_ptr
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Pointer to the most recently received NLB frame buffer. Set by frame dequeue logic, freed after response handler returns.

MEMBER.NAME: tick_count_a
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: GetTickCount snapshot. Updated on connect events (e.g. set to iVar2-8000 in my_handle_connect_to_ssid_response). Purpose: TBD.

MEMBER.NAME: scan_base_ticks
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: GetTickCount captured at scan start (my_start_scan_and_send_beacon). Used to derive scan slot timing windows at +0x920/0x924/0x928/0x92c.

MEMBER.NAME: request_timeout_ms
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Timeout (ms) for current pending request. 3000 ms = scan / BEACON 23000 ms = first scan (param_1 != 0 path) 10000 ms = NETWORKS_LIST, CONNECT, etc.

MEMBER.NAME: pending_flag
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Non-zero while a request frame is pending ACK. Cleared on response or timeout. Zeroed by my_handle_networks_list_response, my_handle_adapter_info_response, etc.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x28
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown (4 bytes).

MEMBER.NAME: hmac_dhcp_buf
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 64-byte multi-purpose buffer. Bytes [0x00..0x0f] = HMAC-SHA1 session message (16 bytes). Read as 4 dwords by xpp_calculate_handshake_hmac. Bytes [0x10..0x3f] = DHCP relay / option buffer (optional secondary). Searched by xpp_dhcp_find_option when bit 0x2000000 of 'this' is set.

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_opt_buf
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 0x80-byte secondary DHCP option buffer. Searched by xpp_dhcp_find_option when bit 0x1000000 of 'this' is set. Also accessed via bit flags in my_handle_adapter_info_response.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0xec
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown (4 bytes, 0xec..0xef).

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_recv_buf
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Primary DHCP receive buffer (64 bytes). Used by xpp_dhcp_find_option as primary search buffer: FUN_0013cabb(this+0xf0, param_size - 0xf0, option_code, ...) Minimum DHCP packet size for this handler = 0xf0 bytes.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x130
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown region (0x80 bytes, 0x130..0x1af). May include: +0x130: ptr used as WEP key object (AutoClass1_clear_connect_flag_wep) +0x1ac: flag byte (checked ==0 in AutoClass1_load_scan_entry_to_cfg)

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x1b0
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown region (0x68 bytes, 0x1b0..0x217). May include: +0x1dc: KeTickCount reference baseline +0x1e0: 6-byte field compared against DHCP packet+0x24 (hardware addr) +0x1e8: ushort used in IP/routing calculations

MEMBER.NAME: snapshot_in_progress
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Set to 1 while snapshot operation is active. Non-zero blocks re-entry. Cleared when snapshot completes. Different from snapshot_pending at +0x112c.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x21c
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown region (0x4c bytes, 0x21c..0x267). May include: +0x21c: pointer (undefined4**) +0x268/0x26c: uint pair compared bitwise in DHCP/FSM logic

MEMBER.NAME: fsm_nonce_a
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: FSM/DHCP nonce value A. Bitwise ANDed with fsm_nonce_b: (fsm_nonce_b & fsm_nonce_a) == xpp_fsm_handle_dhcp_response compare

MEMBER.NAME: fsm_nonce_b
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: FSM/DHCP nonce value B. Paired with fsm_nonce_a for XID/state validation.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x270
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Large unknown buffer (0x630 bytes, 0x270..0x89f). Contains WPA key material, FSM timer state, and TX buffer management. +0x270: FUN_00133737 object (connection object initialised here) +0x294/0x298: uint pairs zeroed on reset +0x29c: self-ptr to +0x2a0 +0x2a8: sub-object pointer Sub-regions TBD from further analysis.

MEMBER.NAME: fsm_timer
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: FSM timer block (0x20 bytes). +0x8a0: xpp_fsm_set_timer target (timer handle) +0x8b0: timer list ptr +0x8b4: timer param_3 (deadline value) +0x8b8: timer self-ptr +0x8bc: FUN_00133767 timer object

MEMBER.NAME: retry_counters
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Retry and attempt counters (8 bytes). +0x8c4: decremented on retry events Other bytes: related retry tracking fields

MEMBER.NAME: fsm_state
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Primary FSM state byte. Key values: 0x04 = DHCP_ACK_WAIT 0x08 = DHCP state 8 0x09 = DHCP state 9 0x0a = DHCP state A 0x0b = DHCP state B (IP ready) 0x0c = IP_READY 0x0d = CONNECTED 0x0e = CONNECTED_DHCP 0x11 = WPA_ASSOC 0x16 = SCAN Read by xpp_build_wpa_assoc_request, xpp_fsm_handle_dhcp_response, etc.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_assoc_retry
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Non-zero = retry WPA association. Checked by xpp_build_wpa_assoc_request.

MEMBER.NAME: connect_retry_count
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Connect retry counter. Incremented on each retry attempt. Checked against limit 0x18 in FSM state 0x09.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x8cb
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown byte.

MEMBER.NAME: fsm_state_flags
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: FSM state flag byte. Individual bits: bit 3 (0x08): IP-ready signal flag (tested in xpp_fsm_handle_dhcp_response) bit 4 (0x10): cleared on DHCP state transitions Other bits TBD.

MEMBER.NAME: auth_flags
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Authentication flags byte. Bit 0x01 checked alongside short at +0x91e.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0x8ce
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown (2 bytes). Copied to outbound frame at offset +0x14.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_eapol_key_data
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA EAPOL key data block (0x20 bytes, 7 dwords used). Dwords at +0x8d0/0x8d4/0x8d8/0x8dc/0x8e0/0x8e4/0x8e8/0x8ec Written from WPA key exchange, swapped with backup region at +0x908..+0x914.

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_wpa_state
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP / WPA state block (0x18 bytes). +0x8f0 (uint): DHCP offered IP address (from DHCP OFFER frame+0x10) +0x8f1: set 0xfe (DHCP client ID marker) +0x8f2/0x8f3: incrementing PRNG counters +0x8f4 (uint): value paired with +0x268 in DHCP comparison +0x8f8/0x8fc/0x900/0x904: WPA key backup dwords

MEMBER.NAME: dns_servers
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DNS server IP addresses (up to 4 x uint32). Populated by xpp_dhcp_find_option scanning DHCP ACK options. Set to 0 before each DHCP parse.

MEMBER.NAME: scan_slot_cfg
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Scan slot configuration (8 bytes). +0x918 (short*): scan channel list iteration pointer +0x91c (ushort): active scan channel (copied from +0x938) +0x91e (short): non-zero enables auth flag check at +0x8cd

MEMBER.NAME: scan_tick_baseline
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Tick count baseline for scan slot timing computation. Set by my_start_scan_and_send_beacon via GetTickCount.

MEMBER.NAME: scan_slot_50pct
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 50% scan interval threshold (ticks). Computed as scan_slot_50pct * 5 + scan_tick_baseline.

MEMBER.NAME: scan_slot_87pct
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 87.5% scan interval threshold (ticks).

MEMBER.NAME: scan_slot_100pct
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 100% scan interval threshold (ticks). Checked for slot expiry.

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_server_ip
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP server IP from DHCP OFFER Option 54 (0x36). Network byte order.

MEMBER.NAME: scan_channel_misc
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Miscellaneous scan channel state (6 bytes). +0x934 (int): non-zero if scan has pending channel requests +0x938 (short): current scan channel number

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_cmp_buf
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: SSID comparison scratch buffer (0x28 bytes). +0x93a: start of target SSID string for scan match Length computed as strlen difference.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_cred_buf0
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA credential buffer 0 (64 bytes). Used in WPA 4-way handshake key derivation.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_cred_buf1
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA credential buffer 1 (64 bytes). Parallel buffer to wpa_cred_buf0 for 4-way handshake.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_key_deriv
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA key derivation working buffer (0x28 bytes). +0x9e2: FUN_0013c9db target (PRF computation, 0x28 bytes output)

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_assoc_ssid
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: SSID string used in WPA_ASSOC_REQ packet (null-terminated, up to 0x29 chars). +0xa0a: string start Length: (pcVar3 - (this+0xa0b)) computed by xpp_build_wpa_assoc_request

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_anonce_ptr
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Pointer to cached ANonce/MIC buffer. Used by xpp_build_wpa_assoc_request when fsm_state != 0x11 (reads *(this->wpa_anonce_ptr)).

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_handshake_flags
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA handshake flag bytes (0x0c bytes). +0xa38: set 1 when ANonce received +0xa39: bit 0x08 checked for MIC validation +0xa3a: cVar1 copy +0xa3b: cVar1 read-back +0xa3c: cleared +0xa3d: set 1

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_ptk_region
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA PTK / MIC region (0x20 bytes). +0xa44 (uint): copied to outbound WPA frame+8 +0xa4c (uint): from WPA assoc response iVar7+0x194 +0xa50 (ushort): from iVar7+0x198 +0xa52 (ushort): from param_1+0x19a +0xa54 (uint): copied to puVar4[0] +0xa58 (ushort): copied to puVar4+1 +0xa5a (ushort): copied to puVar4+3

MEMBER.NAME: fsm_timer_region
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: FSM timing state (0x18 bytes). +0xa60 (uint): set to tick_count_a on certain state transitions +0xa64 (uint): timer comparison value +0xa68: xpp_fsm_set_timer target (second timer) +0xa70 (uint): set 0xffffffff (timer disabled) +0xa74 (ptr): set to LAB_0013f087 (FSM jump target)

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_flags_a
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP state flags byte A (0xa78). Read as uint* by xpp_build_connect_request.

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_flags_b
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP state flags byte B (0xa79). bit 0x20 = DHCP OFFER received bit 0x80 = DHCP ACK received bit 0x10 = set in NAK path

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_error_flags
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP error flags (0xa7a). 0x01 = options exhausted 0x02 = NAK received 0x08 = bad msg type 0x10 = option 0x35 missing 0x20 = option 0x36 invalid 0x40 = no unicast gateway 0x80 = bad lease time

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_retry_flags
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP retry flags (0xa7b). 0x01 = subnet mask invalid 0x02 = wrong FSM state for OFFER 0x04 = wrong FSM state for REQUEST 0x08 = wrong FSM state for ACK 0x80 = retry triggered

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_xid
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP transaction ID (XID, 4 bytes). Used as big-endian value: (v>>24|(v&0xff0000)>>8|(v&0xff00)<<8|v<<24) compared against DHCP packet+0x0c in xpp_fsm_handle_dhcp_response. Also used as state_change_counter in WPA: incremented at +0xa7c+(-1).

MEMBER.NAME: ip_routing_sentinel
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: XPP_RouteEntry circular list sentinel node header (8 bytes). +0xa80 (ptr): next_ptr — initially points to self +0xa84 (ptr): prev_ptr — initially points to self List empty when next_ptr == &this->ip_routing_sentinel.

MEMBER.NAME: routing_state
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: IP routing and network state block (0x48 bytes). +0xa88 (uint): zeroed on route clear +0xa8c (uint): zeroed on route clear +0xa90 (ptr*): routing sub-object ptr A +0xa94 (ptr*): routing sub-object ptr B +0xa98: routing entry base (int)this+0xa98 +0xac8 (ptr*): TX buffer ptr +0xacc (ushort**): TX buffer data ptr +0xad0 (ushort**): RX buffer data ptr +0xad4 (ushort): TX/RX count +0xad8 (uint): TX byte counter +0xadc (uint): RX byte counter

MEMBER.NAME: txrx_event_region
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: TX/RX event and counter region (0x28 bytes). +0xae8 (uint): OR'd with 1 on TX completion +0xaec (void**): thunk function pointer for TX completion +0xaf0 (uint): set to 1 when packet queued +0xaf4 (byte**): TX buffer end pointer for boundary check +0xaf8 (ptr): KeSetEvent target — signalled when IP address ready (state 0x0c)

MEMBER.NAME: packet_buf
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Outbound packet assembly buffer (0x48 bytes). +0xb00: start of buffer iterated during frame build +0xb48 (int*): frame parameter block pointer

MEMBER.NAME: field_0xb4c
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown region (0x6c bytes, 0xb4c..0xbb7).

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_model_name
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Adapter model name ASCII string (33 bytes including null terminator). From HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0x82..0xa2]. Control chars and 0x7f are replaced with 0x00 (sanitized). Example: 'MN-740 802.11b Wireless Adapter'

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_fw_version
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Adapter firmware version ASCII string (33 bytes including null terminator). From HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xa2..0xc2]. Control chars and 0x7f are replaced with 0x00 (sanitized). Example: '1.0.2.26'

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_model_utf16
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: UTF-16LE of adapter_model_name (33 wchar_t = 66 bytes). Generated by my_convert_char_to_wchar_string(this+0xbfa, this+0xbb8, 33).

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_fw_utf16
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: UTF-16LE of adapter_fw_version (33 wchar_t = 66 bytes). Generated by my_convert_char_to_wchar_string(this+0xc3c, this+0xbd9, 33).

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_eth_mac_lo
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Adapter Ethernet MAC bytes [0..3] (4 bytes). Written as dword: *(uint*)this+0xc7e = *(uint*)(frame+6). Copied to XPP_EthFrame.dst_mac[0..3] on every outbound frame.

MEMBER.NAME: adapter_eth_mac_hi
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Adapter Ethernet MAC bytes [4..5] (2 bytes). Written as word: *(ushort*)this+0xc82 = *(ushort*)(frame+10). Copied to XPP_EthFrame.dst_mac[4..5] on every outbound frame.

MEMBER.NAME: rate_list
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Supported 802.11 TX rate codes (up to 14 entries, 0 = list end). Stored as: +0xc84(uint)+0xc88(uint)+0xc8c(uint)+0xc90(ushort) Decoded from HANDSHAKE_RESP capability bitmask at frame[0xca..0xcd]. Validated by AutoClass1_find_rate_in_list.

MEMBER.NAME: channel_list
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Supported 802.11 channel numbers (0xca bytes, up to 202 entries). Decoded from HANDSHAKE_RESP capability bitmap at frame[0xdb..0xe9]. Validated by AutoClass1_find_channel_in_list.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_ibss
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: IBSS (ad-hoc) supported: frame byte[0xea] & 0x02.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_ess
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: ESS (infrastructure) supported: frame byte[0xea] & 0x01.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_privacy
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Privacy (WEP) supported: frame byte[0xea] & 0x04.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_short_preamble
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Short preamble supported: frame byte[0xc8] & 0x02.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_pbcc
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: PBCC (Packet Binary Convolutional Coding): frame byte[0xc8] & 0x04.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_wpa1_rsn
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA1/RSN supported: frame byte[0xc8] & 0x10. GATES WPA PSK menu. Read by xpp_select_best_security_mode as param_2.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_wpa2_agn
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA2/802.11agn supported: frame byte[0xc8] & 0x20. Read by xpp_select_best_security_mode as param_3.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_wep40
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-40 supported: frame byte[0xc9] & 0x01.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_wep104
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-104 supported: frame byte[0xc9] & 0x02.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_wep128_menu
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-128 menu gate: frame byte[0xc9] & 0x04. Non-zero enables the WEP-128 option in the UI security selection menu.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_tkip
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: TKIP supported: frame byte[0xc9] & 0x08.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_ccmp
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: CCMP (AES) supported: frame byte[0xc9] & 0x10.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_wpa_psk
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA-PSK supported: frame byte[0xc9] & 0x20.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_byte_c8
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Raw capability byte from HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xc8]. Source for cap_short_preamble / cap_pbcc / cap_wpa1_rsn / cap_wpa2_agn.

MEMBER.NAME: cap_byte_c9
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Raw capability byte from HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xc9]. Source for cap_wep40..cap_wpa_psk flags.

MEMBER.NAME: radio_connected
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Set to 1 by my_handle_connect_to_ssid_response on successful connect. Also written from HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xf0] (radio active flag).

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0xd93
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Alignment padding byte.

MEMBER.NAME: current_ip
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Current IP address (uint32, host byte order). Written from ADAPTER_INFO_RESP Tag 0x01 payload (4 bytes). Also populated from HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xec] (static IP if DHCP not used).

MEMBER.NAME: dhcp_radio_flag
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: DHCP/radio state flag byte from ADAPTER_INFO_RESP Tag 0x04 payload[0].

MEMBER.NAME: subnet_mask
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Subnet mask bytes (4 bytes, host byte order). From HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xc2..0xc5].

MEMBER.NAME: gateway_ip_hi
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Gateway IP high 2 bytes. From HANDSHAKE_RESP frame[0xc6..0xc7].

MEMBER.NAME: current_ssid_entry
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Type 'XPP_ScanEntry' was deleted; XPP_ScanEntry (0xb4 bytes) for the currently associated network. Populated by XPP_ScanEntry_set_ssid(this+0xda0, frame+0xf6, uVar7) from ADAPTER_INFO_RESP Tag 0x07 payload.

MEMBER.NAME: field_0xeb4
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown (0x10 bytes, 0xeb4..0xec3). +0xec4 is the start of connect_cfg (snapshot source). +0xec8: single byte read in xpp_build_connect_request. +0xec9: current_bssid[6] (see below). These fields may live inside this gap or overlap the cfg start.

MEMBER.NAME: cfg_prefix
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: First 4 bytes of connect_cfg block (0xec4..0xec7). Content TBD. Part of 0x130-byte block snapshotted before CONNECT_REQ.

MEMBER.NAME: cfg_channel_flag
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Single byte read by xpp_build_connect_request for Tag 0x05 (channel/rate). Likely = active channel number or channel-override flag.

MEMBER.NAME: current_bssid_lo
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Current BSSID bytes [0..3]. Written as dword by AutoClass1_update_cfg_bssid_if_changed.

MEMBER.NAME: current_bssid_hi
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Current BSSID bytes [4..5]. Written as word by AutoClass1_update_cfg_bssid_if_changed.

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0xecf
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Padding byte.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_cfg_valid
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 1 when ssid_cfg_bytes is populated. Set by AutoClass1_set_ssid_from_unicode.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_cfg_len
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Length of ssid_cfg_bytes in bytes (0..32).

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_cfg_bytes
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Configured SSID bytes (up to 32 bytes ASCII/raw). Written by AutoClass1_set_ssid_from_unicode from the UI selection. Sent as Tag 0x07 payload in CONNECT_REQ when bitmask bit 0x80 is set.

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0xef8
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 2-byte alignment gap before ssid_cfg_utf16.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_cfg_utf16
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: UTF-16LE of ssid_cfg_bytes (33 wchar_t = 66 bytes, null terminated). Target of _wcscmp in AutoClass1_set_ssid_if_changed. Written by my_convert_char_to_wchar_string(this+0xefa, this+0xed8, len).

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_cfg_display
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Display copy of ssid_cfg_bytes (32 bytes). Written alongside ssid_cfg_bytes in the embedded set_ssid logic at +0x6c.

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0xf5c
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 2-byte alignment gap before enc_type.

MEMBER.NAME: enc_type
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Encryption type for CONNECT_REQ Tag 0x09 (link state encoding): 0x01 = Open (no encryption) 0x02 = WEP-64 0x03 = WEP-128 0x04 = WPA Set by AutoClass1_set_security_wep128 / AutoClass1_set_security_open etc. Encoded to Tag 0x09 wire value by xpp_encode_tag09_link_state.

MEMBER.NAME: auth_alg
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Authentication algorithm for CONNECT_REQ Tag 0x08 (auth type encoding): 0x00 = Open System 0x01 = Shared Key 0x02 = WPA (EAP) Set by AutoClass1_set_shared_key_mode and xpp_encode_tag08_auth_type.

MEMBER.NAME: _gap_0xf60
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unknown region (0x12 bytes, 0xf60..0xf71). Zeroed in blocks of 4 bytes by AutoClass1_set_security_wep128: 0xf60/0xf64/0xf68/0xf6c cleared, 0xf70 byte cleared. +0xf71 (byte): checked against param_1 (WEP key active slot flag?).

MEMBER.NAME: wep64_key_0
wep64_key_1
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-40/64 key slot 1 (5 bytes). Tag 0x0b, bit 0x08.

MEMBER.NAME: wep64_key_2
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-40/64 key slot 2 (5 bytes). Tag 0x0c, bit 0x10.

MEMBER.NAME: wep64_key_3
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-40/64 key slot 3 (5 bytes). Tag 0x0d, bit 0x20. All 4 WEP-64 slots typically contain the same key (UI sets all 4 identically).

MEMBER.NAME: wep128_key
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-128 key (13 bytes). Written: 3x *(uint*) + *(byte*) = 13 bytes. Sent as Tag 0x0f in CONNECT_REQ when +0xff9 bit 0x80 is set.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_pmk
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA PMK (Pairwise Master Key, 32 bytes). Tag 0x10 payload. NOTE: Stock MN-740 firmware v1.0.2.26 IGNORES Tag 0x10 entirely. A patched firmware is required for PMK injection to work.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_passphrase
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA ASCII passphrase (up to 64 bytes, null-terminated). Tag 0x12 payload, sent when +0xffa bit 0x04 is set. Firmware derives PMK internally via PBKDF2-SHA1 from this field.

MEMBER.NAME: connect_pending
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Set to 1 by my_handle_connect_to_ssid_response when connect is confirmed. Cleared (zeroed) once the result has been consumed.

MEMBER.NAME: connect_req_bitmask
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: TLV inclusion bitmask for xpp_build_connect_request (4 bytes). byte 0 (+0xff8): bit 0x80 = include Tag 0x07 (SSID) bit 0x40 = include Tag 0x06 (BSSID) bit 0x20 = include Tag 0x05 (channel/rate) bit 0x08 = include Tag 0x04 (net_mode) byte 1 (+0xff9): bit 0x04 = Tag 0x0a (WEP-64 slot 0) bit 0x08 = Tag 0x0b (WEP-64 slot 1) bit 0x10 = Tag 0x0c (WEP-64 slot 2) bit 0x20 = Tag 0x0d (WEP-64 slot 3) bit 0x40 = Tag 0x0e (WEP default key index) bit 0x80 = Tag 0x0f (WEP-128 key) byte 2 (+0xffa): bit 0x01 = Tag 0x10 (WPA PMK) bit 0x02 = Tag 0x08/auth_alg bit 0x04 = Tag 0x12 (WPA passphrase) byte 3 (+0xffb): reserved

MEMBER.NAME: snapshot_cfg

Copied from this+0xec4 by AutoClass1_snapshot_cfg_for_connect immediately before xpp_build_connect_request is called. Preserves the exact config that was sent in the CONNECT_REQ for comparison in AutoClass1_compare_cfg_block.

MEMBER.NAME: wep128_key
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-128 key (13 bytes). Written: 3x *(uint*) + *(byte*) = 13 bytes. Sent as Tag 0x0f in CONNECT_REQ when +0xff9 bit 0x80 is set.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_pmk
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA PMK (Pairwise Master Key, 32 bytes). Tag 0x10 payload. NOTE: Stock MN-740 firmware v1.0.2.26 IGNORES Tag 0x10 entirely. A patched firmware is required for PMK injection to work.

MEMBER.NAME: wpa_passphrase
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: WPA ASCII passphrase (up to 64 bytes, null-terminated). Tag 0x12 payload, sent when +0xffa bit 0x04 is set. Firmware derives PMK internally via PBKDF2-SHA1 from this field.

MEMBER.NAME: connect_pending
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Set to 1 by my_handle_connect_to_ssid_response when connect is confirmed. Cleared (zeroed) once the result has been consumed.

MEMBER.NAME: connect_req_bitmask
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: TLV inclusion bitmask for xpp_build_connect_request (4 bytes). byte 0 (+0xff8): bit 0x80 = include Tag 0x07 (SSID) bit 0x40 = include Tag 0x06 (BSSID) bit 0x20 = include Tag 0x05 (channel/rate) bit 0x08 = include Tag 0x04 (net_mode) byte 1 (+0xff9): bit 0x04 = Tag 0x0a (WEP-64 slot 0) bit 0x08 = Tag 0x0b (WEP-64 slot 1) bit 0x10 = Tag 0x0c (WEP-64 slot 2) bit 0x20 = Tag 0x0d (WEP-64 slot 3) bit 0x40 = Tag 0x0e (WEP default key index) bit 0x80 = Tag 0x0f (WEP-128 key) byte 2 (+0xffa): bit 0x01 = Tag 0x10 (WPA PMK) bit 0x02 = Tag 0x08/auth_alg bit 0x04 = Tag 0x12 (WPA passphrase) byte 3 (+0xffb): reserved

MEMBER.NAME: snapshot_cfg
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Snapshot copy of connect_cfg block (0x130 bytes = 0x4c dwords). Copied from this+0xec4 by AutoClass1_snapshot_cfg_for_connect immediately before xpp_build_connect_request is called. Preserves the exact config that was sent in the CONNECT_REQ for comparison in AutoClass1_compare_cfg_block.

MEMBER.NAME: snapshot_pending
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Snapshot guard flag (4 bytes). Set to connect_req_bitmask (+0xff8) by AutoClass1_snapshot_cfg_for_connect. Non-zero blocks re-entry into snapshot function (returns 0 immediately). Distinct from snapshot_in_progress (+0x218) which guards the copy loop itself.

MEMBER.NAME: _trail_0x1130
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Trailing bytes to end of verified struct extent (0x1133 bytes total).

MEMBER.NAME: dst_mac
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Destination Ethernet MAC (adapter MAC from AutoClass1+0xc7e).

MEMBER.NAME: src_mac
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Source Ethernet MAC (console MAC from AutoClass1+0x00).

MEMBER.NAME: ethertype
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: EtherType 0x886f (Microsoft NLB Heartbeat).

MEMBER.NAME: xpp_signature
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: XPP magic bytes: 'XBOX' (0x58 0x4f 0x42 0x58).

MEMBER.NAME: version_major
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Always 0x01.

MEMBER.NAME: version_minor
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Always 0x01.

MEMBER.NAME: size_in_dwords
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Payload length in dwords (excludes 14-byte Ethernet header).

MEMBER.NAME: packet_type
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: XPP packet type byte.

MEMBER.NAME: sequence_nonce
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Big-endian frame sequence counter.

MEMBER.NAME: checksum
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: RFC 1071 ones-complement checksum.

MEMBER.NAME: result_code
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Response result byte (0=ok).

MEMBER.NAME: tag_count
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Number of TLV tags following.

MEMBER.NAME: tlv_payload
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Variable TLV payload (up to 0x3e8 bytes = max frame - fixed header).

MEMBER.NAME: dst_mac
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Adapter Ethernet MAC (AutoClass1+0xc7e[4]+0xc82[2]). Set to adapter MAC learned from HANDSHAKE_RESP.

MEMBER.NAME: src_mac
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Console Ethernet MAC (AutoClass1+0x02[6]). Set from source_mac field.

MEMBER.NAME: ethertype
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: EtherType 0x886f — Microsoft NLB Heartbeat (LE on wire = 6F 88).

MEMBER.NAME: xpp_signature
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Magic bytes 0x58 0x4F 0x42 0x58 = ASCII 'XBOX'.

MEMBER.NAME: version_major
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Protocol version major — always 0x01.

MEMBER.NAME: version_minor
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Protocol version minor — always 0x01.

MEMBER.NAME: size_in_dwords
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Payload length in 32-bit words (excludes 14-byte Ethernet header).

MEMBER.NAME: packet_type
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: XPP packet type: 0x01 HANDSHAKE_REQ 0x02 HANDSHAKE_RESP 0x03 NETWORKS_REQ 0x04 NETWORKS_RESP 0x05 ADAPTER_INFO_REQ 0x06 ADAPTER_INFO_RESP 0x07 CONNECT_REQ 0x08 CONNECT_RESP 0x09 BEACON_REQ 0x0a BEACON_RESP 0x0b/0x0c/0x0f DROP_COUNTERx 0x11 WPA_ASSOC_REQ

MEMBER.NAME: sequence_nonce
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Big-endian sequence counter (AutoClass1+0x4a). Incremented per transmitted frame.

MEMBER.NAME: checksum
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: RFC 1071 ones-complement checksum over XPP header+payload. Zero during calculation.

MEMBER.NAME: result_code
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Response result code: 0x00 OK 0x01 error_hard 0x02 retry 0x03 error 0x04 error_connect Always 0x00 in requests.

MEMBER.NAME: tag_count
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Number of TLV tags in payload. 0x00 in error responses.

MEMBER.NAME: frame_data_ptr
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Points to frame_data[0] (this+0x08). Passed to my_make_nlb_frame so it can fill XPP_EthFrame header fields via struct overlay.

MEMBER.NAME: total_frame_len
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Total byte length of frame_data (payload_size + 0x0e). Used for checksum calculation and NLB send registration.

MEMBER.NAME: frame_data
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Ethernet frame bytes. Bytes [0x00..0x1b] = XPP_EthFrame (28 bytes). Bytes [0x1c..0x3f7] = TLV payload (up to 0x3dc bytes).

MEMBER.NAME: next_ptr
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Next node pointer. List empty when next_ptr == &AutoClass1+0xa80 (sentinel).

MEMBER.NAME: prev_ptr
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Previous node pointer.

MEMBER.NAME: ref_count
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Reference count. Set to 1 on allocation.

MEMBER.NAME: route_flags
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Route flags (param_4 to net_remove_ip_routing_entries). Bit 0x0002 = unconditional (bypasses unicast check on dest and gateway IP).

MEMBER.NAME: metric
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Route metric. Secondary sort key (ascending) after subnet_mask. Primary sort: subnet_mask descending (most-specific first).

MEMBER.NAME: dest_ip_masked
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Destination IP address ANDed with subnet_mask (param_1 & param_2).

MEMBER.NAME: subnet_mask
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Subnet mask in host byte order. Primary routing sort key (descending).

MEMBER.NAME: gateway_ip
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Gateway (next-hop) IP address in host byte order.

MEMBER.NAME: scan_index
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Slot counter value at population time (incremented each NETWORKS_RESP parse). Set to 1 in AutoClass1_set_ssid_from_unicode embedded-entry usage.

MEMBER.NAME: is_valid
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 1 = entry populated with valid scan data, 0 = empty slot.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: SSID string bytes (up to 32, NUL-padded). Written by XPP_ScanEntry_set_ssid from wire node bytes +0x08..+0x27.

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0x28
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 2-byte alignment gap before ssid_utf16 at +0x2a.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_utf16
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: UTF-16LE SSID (32 wchar_t = 64 bytes). Written by my_convert_char_to_wchar_string(this+0x2a, this+0x08, len). Used for UI display and string comparison.

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0x6a
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 2-byte alignment gap before ssid_display at +0x6c.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_display
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Second copy of SSID bytes (32 bytes) for display comparison. Written by XPP_ScanEntry_set_ssid at this+0x6c alongside ssid[].

MEMBER.NAME: _gap_0x8c
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Unresolved 8 bytes. No XPP function accesses this range.

MEMBER.NAME: bssid_0
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: BSSID bytes [0..3]. From wire node dword at param_1[0] (byte offset +0x00).

MEMBER.NAME: bssid_4
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: BSSID bytes [4..5]. From wire node ushort at param_1[1]+0 (byte offset +0x04).

MEMBER.NAME: infra_mode
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 0 = infrastructure BSS, 1 = IBSS ad-hoc. From wire node byte offset +0x06. Written then read by AutoClass1_set_infra_mode.

MEMBER.NAME: auth_alg
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Authentication algorithm from wire node byte offset +0x28 (param_1+10 dword). 0x00 = Open System 0x01 = Shared Key 0x02 = WPA Read by AutoClass1_load_scan_entry_to_cfg to configure auth_alg field.

MEMBER.NAME: channel
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 802.11 channel number (1-14). From wire node byte offset +0x29. Validated against AutoClass1.channel_list by AutoClass1_find_channel_in_list.

MEMBER.NAME: rssi_byte1
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Raw RSSI byte 1 from wire[0x2a] (AutoClass1_copy_ssid_to_unicode: wire+0x2a). Paired with rssi_byte2 (+0x9e). Distinct from sort RSSI at +0xa0 (wire[0x2c]).

MEMBER.NAME: rssi_byte2
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: Raw RSSI byte 2 from wire[0x2b] (AutoClass1_copy_ssid_to_unicode: wire+0x2b). Paired with rssi_byte1 (+0x9d). Distinct from sort RSSI at +0xa0 (wire[0x2c]).

MEMBER.NAME: security_type
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: NOT a wire field. Return value of AutoClass1_set_infra_mode(). 0x04 = WPA 0x03 = WEP-128 0x02 = WEP-64 else = Open Derived from cap_wpa1_rsn/cap_wep128_menu capability flags.

MEMBER.NAME: rssi
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: RSSI sort key from wire node byte offset +0x2c (param_1+0xb dword). Used as signed byte by XPP_ScanEntry_compare_rssi for qsort (descending). Same value displayed as signal bars after threshold conversion.

MEMBER.NAME: ssid_copy
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 16-byte SSID copy from wire node bytes +0x2d..+0x3c.

MEMBER.NAME: _pad_0xb1
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: 3-byte alignment padding to reach total size of 0xb4 bytes.

Populates the wireless security type drop-down menu in the Xbox dashboard UI. Reads AutoClass1+0xd70 (cap_wpa1_rsn) to gate the WPA PSK option. Stock MN-740 firmware: byte174=0x06, bit0x10 clear -> WPA PSK option NEVER shown. Called during network setup screen rendering cycle.

Validates that a UTF-16LE input string contains only valid hex characters (0-9, A-F, a-f). param_1 = ushort* (UTF-16LE string). Returns 1 if all chars are valid hex, 0 if not. Called from xpp_ui_process_wep128_key_input to detect hex-format WEP-128 key entry.

Decodes a UTF-16LE two-character hex pair (e.g. L'3', L'F') into a single byte (0x3F). param_1 = ushort* pointing at two UTF-16LE chars. Returns decoded byte value. Called in a loop from xpp_ui_process_wep128_key_input to convert 26-char hex string to 13 raw bytes before passing to AutoClass1_set_wep128_key.

WEP-64 key input handler — called when user confirms key entry on the on-screen keyboard. Accepts either 5 ASCII chars (len==5, taken literally) or 10 hex chars (len==10, hex-decoded). Validates: len==5 (ASCII path) or len==10 AND all valid hex (hex path). Returns 0 on failure. Calls FUN_000a2e12() to set enc_type=WEP64, then FUN_000a2cf5() to mirror key to all 4 slots, then FUN_000a2cd3(1) to set channel=1. SINGLE KEY UI CONFIRMED: There is no multi-key UI. Dashboard always mirrors the one user input across all 4 WEP-64 key buffers (0xf72/0xf77/0xf7c/0xf81).

WEP-128 key input handler — called when user confirms key entry on the on-screen keyboard. Accepts either 13 ASCII chars (len==0xd, taken literally) or 26 hex chars (len==0x1a, hex-decoded). Validates: len==13 (ASCII path) or len==26 AND all valid hex (hex path). Returns 0 on failure. Calls FUN_000a2e3a() to set enc_type=WEP128, then FUN_000a2d32() to write 13-byte key to +0xf86. Single key only — WEP-128 firmware stores one key into all 4 hardware slots via CFG_Set_WEP128_Key_Slot.

WPA key input handler. If input is exactly 64 valid hex chars: hex-decodes to 32-byte PMK, calls FUN_000a2d51 (Tag 0x10). If input is 8-63 printable ASCII: copies raw passphrase, calls FUN_000a2d81 (Tag 0x12). Otherwise returns 0 (invalid). Note: Xbox never runs PBKDF2. Hex path sends pre-computed PMK. ASCII path sends plaintext. Stock firmware handles neither — Tag 0x10 is a stub, Tag 0x12 aborts the TLV parse loop.

Builds 12-byte XPP header into frame buffer
Guards radio/channel/cipher field ranges in HS_RESP
Byte 216 radio guard: rejects if >= 2
Byte 176 channel bitmask rejection guard
Encodes one TLV tag [tag][len][data] into buffer
Writes assembled TLV payload into NLB frame
Tears down the NLB callback registration. Clears: AutoClass1+0x08 (callback ptr), +0xff8 (bitmask), +0xff4 (pending flag). Called on connection teardown before re-registering.

Initializes the Ethernet receive buffer for incoming XPP frames. Calls KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel. Sets AutoClass1+0x14 = &DAT_copied_nlb_frame (the NLB copy buffer pointer). Clears _DAT_buffer_is_full_flag. Called at startup and after each received frame is consumed.
XPP checksum: call site uses my_calculate_checksum(0, xpp_header_ptr, body_dwords*4). RFC 1071 Internet checksum. Checksum field must be zeroed before calculation.

Calculates HMAC for HANDSHAKE_REQ/RESP validation. Inputs: cluster_ip (console IP) + source_mac (adapter MAC). Produces 20-byte HMAC-SHA1 digest; dashboard compares only the FIRST 16 bytes. Key derivation: console IP XOR'd with adapter MAC bytes. Called during HANDSHAKE_REQ construction and HANDSHAKE_RESP validation.

Decodes WPA capability flags from two adapter capability bytes. param_1 points to the AutoClass1 object. Reads +0xba (byte174 caps) masked to 0x36, and +0xbb (byte175 caps) masked to 0x3f. Returns 1 if ALL of: +0xbb & 0x01 (WEP-64), +0xbb & 0x02 (WEP-128), +0xbb & 0x04 (Open) are set, AND NOT (+0xba & 0x20 set with +0xba & 0x10 clear). Returns 0 otherwise (adapter does not report full WPA capability). Used by xpp_select_best_security_mode to gate WPA option in the UI.

NOTE: Previously misnamed 'xpp_handle_handshake_response' in some sessions. Decodes capability bytes 174-175 from HANDSHAKE_RESP into a security mode integer. param_1 = byte174 (WPA/RSN caps): bit0x10=WPA1 present, bit0x20=WPA2 present. param_2 = byte175 (UI menu caps): bit0x04=WEP-128, bit0x02=WEP-64, bit0x01=Open. Reads AutoClass1+0xd70 (cap_wpa1_rsn, set from byte174 bit0x10). Priority: 4=WPA > 3=WEP-128 > 2=WEP-64 > 1=Open. Returns enc_type (1-4) stored at AutoClass1+0xe2e. Called from my_handle_nlb_handshake_response with payload bytes [0x116] and [0x117].

Encodes Tag 0x09 (link/network mode) value for CONNECT_REQ and ADAPTER_INFO_REQ. Reads AutoClass1+0xf5e (enc_type): returns 1 if enc=1, 2 if enc=2, 4 if enc=3, 0 otherwise. Maps internal enc type to XPP protocol link-state byte. Wire-verified: WEP-64 infrastructure = 0x02, WEP-128 infrastructure = 0x04.

Encodes Tag 0x08 (auth type/security mode) value for ADAPTER_INFO_REQ. param_1 = wep_flag (enc_type from +0xf5e), param_2 = net_mode (+0xf5c). wep_flag != 4 -> 0x00 (Open System auth) wep_flag == 4, net_mode != 0 -> 0x10 (Shared Key, infrastructure) wep_flag == 4, net_mode == 0 -> 0x20 (Shared Key, ad-hoc) Wire-verified across all capture logs.

Returns true if adapter is in a connected state with valid RSSI. Checks: AutoClass1+0x0d == 0x01 (connected flag) AutoClass1+0x40 != 0x80000001 (not in error state) AutoClass1+0x48 > -0x48 (RSSI above -72 dBm minimum threshold) Used to gate RSSI-dependent UI display paths.

Alternate RSSI validity check, used in scan/background polling context. Checks AutoClass1+0x5c == 0 AND AutoClass1+0x5d > -0x48 (-72 dBm). Returns true if the alternate (scan-phase) RSSI field is valid and above threshold.

Pre-processes the RSSI byte pair from a BEACON_RESP before storing. param_1 = byte[0] (link_state), param_2 = byte[1] (raw RSSI). Likely implements RSSI smoothing/averaging. Return value discarded by caller. Called at top of xpp_handle_beacon_response before the link_state switch.
Zeroes connect_req_bitmask0 (AutoClass1+0xff8). Sets +0xff4 = 1 (pending flag). Called before rebuilding the full CONNECT_REQ TLV bitmask.
Copies the staged connect config block (+0xffc region) to active cfg (+0xec4). Used to commit pending connection parameters before sending CONNECT_REQ.

Sets the XPP adapter admin/pairing password. Copies password bytes into AutoClass1+0xf60 (up to 17 bytes). Sets connect_req_bitmask to include Tag 0x03 in next CONNECT_REQ. Used to lock the adapter to a specific console (pairing/locking scenario). Wire-verified: tag03 len=10 val='aabbccddee' in lysten_password.log Pkt#9.
Compares 0x23 DWORDs (140 bytes) starting at this+0xed0 against param_2. Returns non-zero if blocks differ. Used for change detection before CONNECT_REQ.
Searches the adapter supported channel list (this+0xc92, up to 200 entries). param_1 = channel byte. Returns 1 if found, 0 if channel not supported by adapter.
Searches the adapter supported rate list (this+0xc84, up to 14 entries). param_1 = rate byte. Returns 1 if found, 0 if rate not supported by adapter.
Sets the target 802.11 channel (AutoClass1+0xf71) from param_1. Sets +0xff9 bit 0x40 to include Tag 0x05 (channel) in next CONNECT_REQ. No-op if param_1 matches current channel value at +0xf71.

Mirrors a 5-byte WEP-40/WEP-64 key into all 4 WEP key slots. Writes to AutoClass1+0xf72 (slot 0), +0xf77 (slot 1), +0xf7c (slot 2), +0xf81 (slot 3). Sets +0xff9 bits 0x04|0x08|0x10|0x20 to include Tags 0x0a-0x0d in CONNECT_REQ. NOTE: Dashboard only exposes one WEP-64 key input field. All 4 slots get the same key.

Copies a 13-byte WEP-128 ASCII key into AutoClass1+0xf86..+0xf92. Writes as: 3x DWORD (12 bytes) + 1 BYTE (byte 12) = 13 bytes total. Sets +0xff9 bit 0x80 to include Tag 0x0f (WEP-128 key) in next CONNECT_REQ. Called from xpp_ui_process_wep128_key_input after hex decoding (if input was hex).

Copies a 32-byte raw WPA PMK into AutoClass1+0xf93. Writes 8 DWORDs in a loop from param_1 into this+0xf93..+0x1b2. Sets bit 0x10000 in +0xff8 to include Tag 0x10 (PMK) in CONNECT_REQ. NOTE: Stock MN-740 firmware v1.0.2.26 ignores Tag 0x10 — no case 0x10 in the firmware TLV parser. WPA PMK patch required to use this path. Previously misnamed AutoClass1_set_wep128_key in a prior Ghidra session.

Validates and copies a WPA ASCII passphrase (8-63 chars) into AutoClass1+0xfb3. Validates: 8 <= len <= 63 AND all bytes are printable ASCII. Sets +0xffa bit 0x04 to include Tag 0x12 (WPA passphrase) in next CONNECT_REQ.
Sets enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) = 0x01 (Open/no encryption). Clears WEP/WPA bits from connect_req_bitmask0 (+0xff8).
Sets enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) = 0x02 (WEP-64). Updates connect_req_bitmask0 to include WEP-64 tag bits.

Sets enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) = 0x03 (WEP-128). Updates connect_req_bitmask0 (+0xff8) with WEP-128 tag bits (& 0xfffa83ff | 0x300). Guards: only writes if enc_type != 0x03 already. Called by AutoClass1_load_scan_entry_to_cfg when XPP_ScanEntry.security_type == 0x03. NOTE: Despite old name 'set_wpa_pmk', no PMK operations are performed here. Compare: AutoClass1_set_security_wpa writes 0x04 with a different bitmask.
Sets enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) = 0x04 (WPA). Updates connect_req_bitmask0 to include WPA tag bits.
Sets auth algorithm (AutoClass1+0xf5f) = 0x01 (Shared Key). Sets +0xffa bit 0x02 to flag auth algorithm change for CONNECT_REQ.
Sets auth algorithm (AutoClass1+0xf5f) = 0x00 (Open System). Sets +0xffa bit 0x02 to flag auth algorithm change for CONNECT_REQ.
Sets auth algorithm (AutoClass1+0xf5f) = 0x02 (WPA). Sets +0xffa bit 0x02 to flag auth algorithm change for CONNECT_REQ.
Clears bit 6 (0x40) of connect_req_bitmask0 (AutoClass1+0xff8). Removes Tag 0x06 (BSSID) from the next CONNECT_REQ.
Sets +0xf5c = 1 (Shared Key auth mode). Updates connect_req_bitmask0 (+0xff8) to flag auth mode change.

Downgrades security to Open if WPA is selected but adapter has no WPA1 capability. Checks enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) == 0x04 AND cap_wpa1_rsn (+0xd70) == 0. If true: calls AutoClass1_set_security_open() to revert. Stock MN-740 firmware always returns cap_wpa1_rsn = 0.

Compares 6-byte BSSID at param_1 against cfg_bssid (AutoClass1+0xec9). If different: copies new BSSID to +0xec9, sets bit 0x40 in +0xff8 to include Tag 0x06 (BSSID) in the next CONNECT_REQ. Called from AutoClass1_load_scan_entry_to_cfg with entry->bssid_first4 at +0x94.
Returns true if current enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) == 0x01 (Open).
Returns true if current enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) == 0x02 (WEP-64).
Returns true if current enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) == 0x03 (WEP-128).
Returns true if current enc_type (AutoClass1+0xf5e) == 0x04 (WPA).

Copies 0x4c DWORDs (304 bytes) from the RX/adapter-received state block at AutoClass1+0xd94 into the local config shadow block at +0xec4. Syncs what the adapter last reported into the cfg that will be sent back.
Copies 0x4c DWORDs (304 bytes) from the local cfg block (AutoClass1+0xec4) back into the RX state block at +0xd94. Reverse direction of AutoClass1_copy_rx_state_to_cfg.

Converts raw RSSI byte (signed) to 0-5 signal bar count for UI display. Guards: AutoClass1+0x0d == 0x01 (connected) AND +0x40 != 0x80000001 (no error). Source-verified thresholds (from FUN_000a2fea decompile): 0 bars: rssi <= -91 dBm (0xA5 / -0x5b) 1 bar: rssi <= -82 dBm (0xAE / -0x52) 2 bars: rssi <= -72 dBm (0xB8 / -0x48) 3 bars: rssi <= -68 dBm (0xBC / -0x44) 4 bars: rssi <= -58 dBm (0xC6 / -0x3a) 5 bars: rssi > -58 dBm

Zeroes an XPP_ScanEntry structure in place. Clears the first 2 DWORDs (scan_index, is_valid), then 8 DWORDs (ssid block), 1 trailing byte, and 0x10 DWORDs + 2 bytes (remaining scan fields up to +0x6a), plus the final 8-DWORD block. Total clear: matches XPP_ScanEntry size (0xb4 bytes). Called from XPP_ScanEntry_set_ssid before writing new data.

Sanitizes the SSID byte string in an XPP_ScanEntry. Iterates from param_1+0x08 (ssid field) up to ssid_len (from param_1+0x04). Replaces any byte < 0x20 (control chars) or 0x7f-0xa0 (DEL/non-printable) with 0x20 (space). Zeroes all bytes past the first NUL. Called from XPP_ScanEntry_set_ssid after copying raw SSID bytes.

Initializes an XPP_ScanEntry from a raw scan config block. Clears 0x2d DWORDs (= 0xb4 bytes) in this, then: Writes param_3 (scan_index DWORD) to offset +0x00. Writes param_2 (uint8 wpa_caps flag) to offset +0xa0. Copies 0x23 DWORDs (0x8c bytes) from param_1 into this+0x08. Sets is_valid (offset +0x04) = 1. Used to populate a scan_entries[] slot from a parsed NETWORKS_RESP TLV node.

Compares two XPP_ScanEntry objects by RSSI (signed byte at +0xa0). Returns 0xffffffff if this->rssi < other->rssi (this sorts before other = better signal). Returns 0 if equal, 1 if this->rssi > other->rssi. Used as the comparison predicate for qsort of scan_entries[].

qsort comparison thunk that wraps XPP_ScanEntry_compare_rssi. Swaps param_1 and param_2 before calling: passes (param_2, param_1). This reverses the sort order to produce highest RSSI first (descending). Passed as the comparator function pointer to qsort().

Sets infrastructure/ad-hoc mode. param_1 = 1 for infrastructure, 0 for ad-hoc. Writes to AutoClass1+0xe2c. Updates bitmask for Tag 0x04 (operating mode). Also modifies capability mask bytes at +0x9d and +0x9e.

NLB receive callback. Validates and copies an incoming NLB frame. Called by the NLB driver layer when an 0x886f ethertype frame arrives. Checks _DAT_buffer_is_full_flag to prevent overwrite of unread frame. Copies frame bytes into DAT_copied_nlb_frame buffer. Sets _DAT_buffer_is_full_flag = 1 to signal frame ready for xpp_nlb_frame_dequeue_and_prepare.
ECX now stores the whole frame size

Allocates and initializes an XPP_FrameBuffer for an outgoing packet. param_1 = AutoClass1 ptr, param_2 = payload_size in bytes. Guard: returns NULL if param_2 >= 0x3ef (buffer overflow protection). Allocates 0x404 bytes via XAPILIB::LocalAlloc. Sets frame_data_ptr = &alloc+0x08 (frame_data field). Writes dst_mac from adapter MAC at AutoClass1+0xc7e. Writes src_mac from console MAC at AutoClass1+0x00. Writes ethertype = 0x886f (NLB). Returns XPP_FrameBuffer* or NULL on alloc failure.
size of handshake request wo padding
MS NLB Heartbeat type

Finalizes an XPP_FrameBuffer and transmits it via the NLB layer. param_1 = AutoClass1 ptr, param_2 = XPP_FrameBuffer* to transmit. Sets XPP header fields: signature, version, size_in_dwords, sequence_nonce. Computes RFC 1071 checksum via my_calculate_checksum. Passes completed frame to NLB send function. Frees XPP_FrameBuffer via XAPILIB::LocalFree.

Validates an XPP packet against a pending request. Checks XPP magic (param_1[6] == expected type byte). For ECHO (type 0x05): checks response type byte at param_1[0x25]. Computes and verifies RFC 1071 checksum via my_calculate_checksum. Returns (uint64) with low DWORD = 1 on match, 0 on mismatch. Called from xpp_nlb_frame_dequeue_and_prepare.

Dequeues the next received NLB frame from the copy buffer and prepares it as an XPP_FrameBuffer for dispatch. Reads DAT_copied_nlb_frame_pointer to check for available frames. Calls my_prepare_eth_frame to allocate a buffer and copies frame bytes into it. Calls xpp_nlb_frame_validate_and_match to verify XPP magic/checksum/nonce. Returns XPP_FrameBuffer* on success, NULL if no frame available or invalid.

Builds Type 0x01 HANDSHAKE_REQ packet. Allocates XPP_FrameBuffer via my_prepare_eth_frame(param_1, 0x1c). Payload is 28 bytes: cluster_ip (4) + source_mac (6) + HMAC-SHA1 first 16 bytes. HMAC computed by xpp_calculate_handshake_hmac. Sets packet_type = 0x01. Destination: FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF (broadcast).

Thin bool wrapper over xpp_select_best_security_mode. Calls xpp_select_best_security_mode(this, param_1=cap_byte_174, param_2=cap_byte_175) and returns (result != 0) as a bool. Called from my_handle_nlb_handshake_response during capability validation. Returns false only if xpp_select_best_security_mode returns 0 (no valid mode found). See xpp_select_best_security_mode for full security mode priority logic.

Builds and sends Type 0x03 NETWORKS_LIST_REQ. Allocates XPP_FrameBuffer via my_prepare_eth_frame(param_1, 0x0c). Sets packet_type = 0x03 at frame_data_ptr->packet_type. Sets param_1+0x0c = 2 (request state), param_1+0x20 = 10000 (timeout ticks). Sets param_1+0x40 = 0xffff (retry limit), param_1+0x24 = 1 (pending flag). Saves XPP_FrameBuffer ptr at param_1+0x28. Calls my_make_nlb_frame to finalize and transmit.

Resets NLB frame-receive state to idle. Zeroes timer fields at param_1+0x20 and param_1+0x24. Calls my_setup_eth_buffer(param_1) to reinitialize the receive buffer. Sets param_1+0xc = 0 (clears pending-request flag). Used at the end of a completed request-response cycle.

Builds and transmits Type 0x09 BEACON_REQ. Allocates XPP_FrameBuffer via my_prepare_eth_frame(param_1, 0x0c). Sets packet_type = 0x09. Calls my_make_nlb_frame to finalize and send. Frees XPP_FrameBuffer via XAPILIB::LocalFree after transmission. Called by my_start_scan_and_send_beacon after scan state is initialised.

Handles Type 0x0A BEACON_RESP from the adapter. param_1 = XPP_FrameBuffer*. *param_1 (= frame_data_ptr) is the raw frame byte buffer. Body must be exactly 4 bytes. Valid body[0] range: 0x00-0x03 (CMP/JA guard). Calls xpp_beacon_rssi_preprocess(byte[0], byte[1]) before switch. Stores results into AutoClass1 fields: +0x3c = link_state (from byte[0] switch: 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x03) +0x40 = 0x00000000 (EDX permanently zeroed) +0x44 = is_infrastructure (SETNZ on state != 0x03) +0x48 = RSSI signed value (if byte[1] >= 0xa6) +0x49 = raw byte[2]

Calls AutoClass1_copy_rx_state_to_cfg to sync adapter state to cfg block. Then zeroes connect_req_bitmask0 (+0xff8) and pending flag (+0xff4). Called after a CONNECT_RESP is processed to clear the pending-send state.

Guards on param_1+0x112c (pending snapshot flag): returns 0 if already set. Copies 0x4c DWORDs from cfg block (+0xec4) to staged block (+0xffc). Saves connect_req_bitmask0 (+0xff8) to +0x112c. Calls AutoClass1_copy_rx_state_to_cfg to freeze current adapter state. Returns 1 on success. Called just before xpp_build_connect_request.

Builds Type 0x07 CONNECT_TO_SSID_REQ packet. Bitmask-driven TLV serialiser reading connect_req_bitmask0/1/2: +0xff8 bit 0x80 -> Tag 0x07 (SSID) +0xff8 bit 0x40 -> Tag 0x06 (BSSID) +0xff8 bit 0x20 -> Tag 0x05 (channel/rate) +0xff9 bit 0x04 -> Tag 0x0a (WEP-64 slot 0, 5 bytes @ +0xf72) +0xff9 bit 0x08 -> Tag 0x0b (WEP-64 slot 1, 5 bytes @ +0xf77) +0xff9 bit 0x10 -> Tag 0x0c (WEP-64 slot 2, 5 bytes @ +0xf7c) +0xff9 bit 0x20 -> Tag 0x0d (WEP-64 slot 3, 5 bytes @ +0xf81) +0xff9 bit 0x80 -> Tag 0x0f (WEP-128 key, 13 bytes @ +0xf86) +0xffa bit 0x01 -> Tag 0x10 (PMK, 32 bytes @ +0xf93) [firmware ignores] +0xffa bit 0x04 -> Tag 0x12 (WPA passphrase @ +0xfb3) Also includes Tags 0x01,0x03,0x04,0x08,0x09,0x11 unconditionally.

Handles Type 0x08 CONNECT_RESP from the adapter. param_1 = XPP_FrameBuffer*. *param_1 (= frame_data_ptr) is the raw frame byte buffer. Parses CONNECT_RESP result code and TLV payload. On success: calls AutoClass1_sync_rx_state_and_clear_bitmask to clear pending flags. Advances FSM state based on result code.

Sets the target channel or rate byte in the connection config. Selects channel/rate path based on +0xf5f auth_algorithm flag (0x01 = channel path). Validates param_1 against AutoClass1_find_channel_in_list or _find_rate_in_list. Returns 0 if not supported. Sets bit 0x20 in +0xff8 and writes byte to +0xf5d. No-op if param_1 == current value at +0xf5d.

Loads a selected XPP_ScanEntry from scan_entries[] into the active config. param_1 = XPP_ScanEntry* (entry from AutoClass1+0x78 array, stride 0xb4). Validates channel via AutoClass1_find_channel_in_list. Validates rate via AutoClass1_find_rate_in_list. Returns 0 if either unsupported by adapter. Sets auth_algo from entry+0x9b: 0=Open, 1=SharedKey, 2=WPA. Sets enc_type from entry+0x9f: 0=Open, 2=WEP-64, 3=WEP-128, 4=WPA. Sets infra/ad-hoc from entry+0x9a. Calls AutoClass1_set_shared_key_mode if needed. If duplicate SSID count > 1: calls AutoClass1_update_cfg_bssid_if_changed.

Builds Type 0x05 ADAPTER_INFO_REQ packet. Always sends exactly 9 TLV tags: 0x01,0x02,0x04,0x05,0x06,0x07,0x08,0x09,0x11. Fixed payload = 0x2e (46) bytes. tag_count byte = 0x09. Source AutoClass1 offsets: Tag 0x01 = IP address @ +0xd94 Tag 0x02 = link state @ +0xd98 Tag 0x04 = radio mode @ +0xe2c Tag 0x05 = channel @ +0xe2d Tag 0x06 = BSSID @ +0xec9 Tag 0x07 = SSID_len @ +0xed4, SSID @ +0xf3c Tag 0x08 = auth type via xpp_encode_tag08_auth_type() Tag 0x09 = link state via xpp_encode_tag09_link_state() Tag 0x11 = auth mode from AutoClass1 auth_mode field

Writes an SSID string and length into an XPP_ScanEntry. Clears the entry first via XPP_ScanEntry_clear. Copies up to 0x20 bytes of param_1 into both the raw ssid field (+0x08) and the display copy at +0x6c. Sets is_valid_len (+0x04) = param_2. Calls XPP_ScanEntry_sanitize_ssid to remove control characters. Calls my_convert_char_to_wchar_string to produce UTF-16LE copy at +0x2a. Sets scan_index (+0x00) = 1 (marks slot as populated).
Copies a UTF-16LE SSID string from param_1 into AutoClass1 SSID buffer. Converts UTF-16LE to ASCII/bytes. Sets SSID length field.
Converts SSID from ASCII (cfg_ssid_buf) to UTF-16LE at +0xefa. Calls my_convert_char_to_wchar_string internally.

Handles Type 0x02 HANDSHAKE_RESP from the adapter. param_1 = XPP_FrameBuffer*. *param_1 (= frame_data_ptr) is the raw frame byte buffer. Validates copyright string, HMAC, capability bytes [0xf0..0xf5], [0xea..0xec], [0xeb]. Calls xpp_store_hw_version (= xpp_resolve_security_mode) with bytes [0x116] and [0x117]. On success: stores adapter MAC, cap flags, channel/rate lists, model string, SSID. Sets AutoClass1+0xd = 1 (is_connected), +0x0c = 0, +0x40 = 0, +0x44 = 1.
Adapter firmware version
Copy both adapter name and FW at once
SSID string size
SSID returned in handshake response

Handles Type 0x04 NETWORKS_LIST_RESP from the adapter. param_1 = XPP_FrameBuffer*. *param_1 (= frame_data_ptr) is the raw frame byte buffer. Validates packet_type == 0x04 and body size against network count. Each wire node = 0x3d bytes. Validates per-node: ssid_len <= 0x20, infra_mode <= 1, enc_mode <= 2, channel <= 200, ssid null-termination integrity. Calls AutoClass1_copy_ssid_to_unicode for each valid node into scan_entries[] at AutoClass1+0x78. Clears scan_entries array (0x2d0 dwords = 16 * 0xb4 bytes) before populating. Sets AutoClass1+0x74 = number of valid entries found. NOTE: Does NOT call qsort here — sorting is done by my_handle_networks_list_response caller.

Scan initiator wrapper. Configures scan state then calls my_send_beacon_request. Sets this+0x44=0, this+0x58=0, this+0xc=5 (state=SCAN). Timeout: this+0x20 = 3000ms (param_1==0) or 23000ms (param_1!=0). Seeds RSSI: this+0x5c=0xff, this+0x5d=0x80. Records GetTickCount into this+0x1c (scan_base_ticks).

Compares param_1 (wchar_t* SSID) against cached SSID at AutoClass1+0xefa. If different: calls AutoClass1_set_ssid_from_unicode to copy new SSID to +0xed0. Sets bit 0x80 in connect_req_bitmask0 (+0xff8) to include SSID tag in CONNECT_REQ. Returns 1 always (even if unchanged).

Handles Type 0x06 ADAPTER_INFO_RESP from the adapter. param_1 = XPP_FrameBuffer*. *param_1 (= frame_data_ptr) is the raw frame byte buffer. Validates an IP address for use as a DHCP-assigned or static address. Called from FSM DHCP handling when AutoClass1 IP field is non-zero. Used to gate whether a stored/offered IP is suitable before applying it. param_1 = char* IP string or raw IP dword (needs further decompile to confirm).
Writes deadline tick value to AutoClass1+0xa68. All state timeout scheduling routes through here.

Pseudo-random number generator for nonce/IP generation. Calls FUN_00133c57(param_1, &local_8, 4) to fill 4 random bytes. Returns pointer to the 4-byte result. Used in FSM state 0x18 (link-local IP retries): generates random 3rd and 4th octets for 169.254.x.x address (each mod 0xfe + 1). Also used for WPA nonce generation.

Routing and packet allocation dispatcher (7-param form). Dispatches network packets to the appropriate handler based on param_2 flags. param_1 = pool tag (e.g. 0x7154454e='NET q', 0x7654454e='NET v'). param_2 = packet flags/type bitmask (low 3 bits = uVar3 = packet class). param_3 = packet size. param_4/5/6 = additional routing parameters. Allocates route entries, validates unicast IP via net_validate_unicast_ip. Called from WPA key exchange, DHCP, ARP, and IP routing paths.
Returns 1 if the given IP address is a valid routable unicast address. Rejects: 0.0.0.0 (unset), 255.x.x.x (broadcast), 127.x.x.x (loopback), 224-239.x.x.x (multicast).
If pointer isn't aligned to 2 byte boundary
Writes the byte to AH
current_pointer is stored in ESI
size_in_words is also stored in ECX
If size was odd, writes the last byte to AL
if the size is now 0, exit
keep aligning to the 2 byte boundary...
...until here
now we're going through the buffer in dwords
current value goes into EDX
switch is EBX
add the following `switch` number of dwords
update the pointer
make another unwinded loop iteration
add all the sum to the original variable
add carry bit if there's one
add remaining word if there's one
add together low and high word

Adds/updates entries in IP routing table (circular doubly-linked list at AutoClass1+0xa80). Sentinel = &AutoClass1+0xa80. Allocates XPP_RouteEntry (0x1c bytes, pool tag 0x3754454e=NET7). Validates dest and gateway IPs via net_validate_unicast_ip unless param_4 bit2 set. Checks subnet_mask is contiguous (uVar5 & uVar5+1 == 0). Searches list for existing entry matching (dest_ip_masked, subnet_mask, gateway_ip). Found: unlinks for re-insertion at correct position. Not found: allocates new XPP_RouteEntry node. Inserts sorted: subnet_mask descending (most-specific first), metric (param_5) ascending. Invalidates route cache (+0xa88/+0xa8c) on every call. Signature: (this, dest_ip, subnet_mask, gateway_ip, route_flags, metric).

WPA peer key exchange handler. Adds or updates a peer in the WPA key table. param_1 = byte* key material. Dispatches on *param_1 & 0xe0: 0x00 = full DH: FUN_00133c57 generates nonce, XcModExp computes shared secret. 0x80 = skip DH (jump directly to KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel path). 0xe0 = skip DH. Peer table base ptr: this+0xac8, count: this+0xad4, max: this+0xd. Each entry is 0xf4 bytes: [+0x00]=key[8] [+0x08]=param_2 [+0x10..0x2f]=DH nonce [+0x30..0x4f]=XcModExp result [+0xf0]=flags. Returns WSA error codes: 0x2726=bad param, 0x2776=table full, 0x2735=duplicate peer.
Stops the FSM timer by clearing the deadline at AutoClass1+0xa68. Frees the ANonce/MIC cache buffer at AutoClass1+0xa34. Called on connection teardown and fatal error paths.
Length-bounded SSID copy with null-pad
Assembles 139-byte HMAC input: nonce+MAC+masterkey
RFC 1071 checksum over arbitrary byte range

Resets FSM to idle state. Called from states 0x00, 0x05, 0x16, 0x1b. Guards on AutoClass1+0xa78 bit to prevent re-entrant cleanup. Snapshots scan timing state (+0x908..+0x914) to backup (+0x8d0..+0x8dc). Calls net_remove_ip_routing_entries to flush IP routing table. Clears: IP address, DHCP state, WPA keys, error flags.

Copies AutoClass1 FSM/connection state into XNetConfigParams output buffer. param_1=0: returns bit3 of this+0x8cc (IP_ready flag). param_1!=0: copies frame buffer (this+0xa54/a58/a5a) and slot timing snapshot. Raises IRQL to DPC during copy. Previously misnamed net_prng.
Sets short-duration FSM timer (thiscall, int+short)
FSM abort handler for retry-exceeded states (0x04,0x08,0x0a,0x0d,0x0e,0x0f).

Searches a DHCP packet options field for a specific DHCP option code. Walks the options byte-by-byte. Returns pointer to option data field, or NULL. Used by xpp_fsm_handle_dhcp_response to extract subnet/router/lease options.
Builds Type 0x11 WPA_ASSOC_REQ. Sub-TLV 0x0101: SSID from +0xa0a. Sub-TLV 0x0103: state_change_counter from +0xa7c.

Parses one sub-TLV record from an inbound type 0x11 frame. Called in a loop by xpp_wpa_inbound_frame_handler. Signature: (this, tlv_ptr, frame_type_word, direction, output_ptr, has_output)
Returns: 0 = malformed/unrecognised -> caller aborts loop 1 = skip / ignored 2 = consumed, reply written via output_ptr 3 = consumed, no reply
Dispatch by (tag, frame_type):
frame_type 0x21c0 or 0x23c0: tag=0x01 len=4: IP address dir=1: store confirmed IP -> +0xa40 dir!=1: store proposed IP -> +0xa3e, or error bit 0x02 @ +0xa39 tag=0x05 len=6: DHCP nonce dir=1 + matches +0xa44: reply 0x05/6/NOT(value) -> return 2 dir!=1: net_prng() -> +0xa44 tag=0x03 len>=4: challenge/response len=4 + 0x23c0 -> challenge match len=5 + 0x23c2 + byte[4]=0x05 -> response match match+write: reply 0x03/5/[0x23c2,0x05] -> return 2 else: set bits 0x04/0x08 into +0xa39
frame_type 0x2180 (post-auth IP config): tag=0x03 len=6: gateway -> AutoClass1+0x8f0 tag=0x81 len=6: DNS1 -> AutoClass1+0x8f8 tag=0x83 len=6: DNS2 -> AutoClass1+0x8fc all via net_validate_unicast_ip

Main FSM action dispatcher for the XPP connection state machine. Called on every state transition and on timer tick expiry. Switch 1 (switchD_0013d9f2) — action dispatch on AutoClass1+0x8c8 state: 0x00,0x05,0x16,0x1b -> xpp_fsm_reset_cleanup() 0x02,0x07,0x0b -> net_dispatch_arp() 0x03 -> my_send_networks_list_request() 0x09 -> RETRY GUARD: if +0x8c9!=0 OR ++retry_count(+0x8ca)>=0x18 -> abort 0x0c -> KeSetEvent(+0xaf8) — IP ready signal to dashboard IP stack 0x12 -> xpp_build_wpa_assoc_request() 0x14 -> xpp_fsm_wpa_credential_exchange() 0x18 -> RFC 3927 link-local: 169.254.[MAC_even_xor].[MAC_odd_xor] Switch 2 (switchD_0013dbbc) — timeout scheduler (200ms tick units): 0x0c -> 50% of beacon scan slot (+0x928) 0x0d -> 87.5% (binary-approach adaptive, floored by +0x1f) 0x0e -> 100% (target slot +0x928)
Initialises WPA sub-states 0x11-0x15. Loads WPA credentials from profile into AutoClass1+0x962/0x9a2/0x9e2.

Handles FSM state transitions when a valid XPP response is received. Transition table (confirmed from FUN_0013de56 decompile): state 0x02 -> 0x00 (HANDSHAKE_RESP received) state 0x03 -> 0x04 (NETWORKS_RESP received, networks found) state 0x03 -> 0x05 (NETWORKS_RESP received, no networks) state 0x07 -> 0x09 (CONNECT_RESP success) state 0x0b -> 0x0f (ADAPTER_INFO_RESP received) state 0x18/0x19 -> 0x1a (link-local IP ARP probe complete) Increments state_change_counter (+0xa7c) for replay protection.

FSM timer tick handler. Called every 200ms by the system timer. Checks if tick count has reached deadline at AutoClass1+0xa68. If expired: calls xpp_fsm_state_dispatch with current FSM state. Manages scan slot timing advancement for beacon states 0x0c/0x0d/0x0e.

Entry point for a new XPP wireless connection sequence. Sets FSM state to 0x01. Clears error flags at AutoClass1+0xa78. Calls my_prepare_handshake_request to send initial HANDSHAKE_REQ. Configures initial timeout for HANDSHAKE_RESP wait.

Sets the FSM error flag and re-dispatches to trigger cleanup. param_1 = error code (e.g. 0xc0000000). ORs param_1 into AutoClass1+0xa78 error flags. If current state == 0x14 (WPA handshake): adds 0x80010000 to error flags. Then calls xpp_fsm_state_dispatch(this, 0, 0) to force state 0 cleanup.

Handles an incoming DHCP packet (OFFER, ACK, or NAK). Validates DHCP magic cookie 0x63538263. OFFER: stores offered IP, sends DHCP REQUEST. ACK: extracts subnet mask, router IP, lease time via xpp_dhcp_find_option. Calls net_remove_ip_routing_entries to install routes. Signals ip_ready_event via KeSetEvent(AutoClass1+0xaf8). NAK: resets DHCP state, triggers retry.

Top-level handler for inbound type 0x11 frames sent BY THE ADAPTER. Console must be in FSM state >= 0x13 to accept -- frames arriving in state 0x11/0x12 are silently discarded.
Entry guards (bail to FUN_0013ee4f = discard on any failure): [EDI+4] payload length word must be >= 4 Byte-swapped length must fit within declared length AutoClass1+0x8c8 (FSM state) must be >= 0x13 Sub-type byte [ESI+0] must not be 0x05, 0x07, or 0x08
Sub-type routing: 0x09 = ANonce delivery frame_type must be 0x21c0, len>=8, +0xa38 must == 0x04 -> xpp_wpa_outbound_frame_builder with tag=0x0a + ANonce 0x01-0x04 = IP/DHCP negotiation read pass: loop sub-TLVs via xpp_wpa_subtlv_parser if sub-type==0x01 and FSM==0x14: xpp_fsm_wpa_state_setup(0x13) sets bit 0x04 in AutoClass1+0xa7a write pass: second loop generates reply sub-TLVs sends reply via xpp_wpa_outbound_frame_builder local_10[0]==0x02 -> 0x04, xpp_fsm_wpa_state_setup(0x14/0x15)
Frame type sub-protocols (word inside payload): 0x21c0 = DHCP/IP negotiation + WPA challenge handshake 0x23c0 = WPA 4-way ANonce/SNonce exchange 0x2180 = Post-auth IP configuration delivery

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_ui_populate_security_menu
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Populates the wireless security type drop-down menu in the Xbox dashboard UI. Reads AutoClass1+0xd70 (cap_wpa1_rsn) to gate the WPA PSK option. Stock MN-740 firmware: byte174=0x06, bit0x10 clear -> WPA PSK option NEVER shown. Called during network setup screen rendering cycle.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_validate_hex_string
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Validates that a UTF-16LE input string contains only valid hex characters (0-9, A-F, a-f). param_1 = ushort* (UTF-16LE string). Returns 1 if all chars are valid hex, 0 if not. Called from xpp_ui_process_wep128_key_input to detect hex-format WEP-128 key entry.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_decode_hex_byte_pair
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Decodes a UTF-16LE two-character hex pair (e.g. L'3', L'F') into a single byte (0x3F). param_1 = ushort* pointing at two UTF-16LE chars. Returns decoded byte value. Called in a loop from xpp_ui_process_wep128_key_input to convert 26-char hex string to 13 raw bytes before passing to AutoClass1_set_wep128_key.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_ui_process_wep64_key_input
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-64 key input handler — called when user confirms key entry on the on-screen keyboard. Accepts either 5 ASCII chars (len==5, taken literally) or 10 hex chars (len==10, hex-decoded). Validates: len==5 (ASCII path) or len==10 AND all valid hex (hex path). Returns 0 on failure. Calls FUN_000a2e12() to set enc_type=WEP64, then FUN_000a2cf5() to mirror key to all 4 slots, then FUN_000a2cd3(1) to set channel=1. SINGLE KEY UI CONFIRMED: There is no multi-key UI. Dashboard always mirrors the one user input across all 4 WEP-64 key buffers (0xf72/0xf77/0xf7c/0xf81).

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_ui_process_wep128_key_input
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: WEP-128 key input handler — called when user confirms key entry on the on-screen keyboard. Accepts either 13 ASCII chars (len==0xd, taken literally) or 26 hex chars (len==0x1a, hex-decoded). Validates: len==13 (ASCII path) or len==26 AND all valid hex (hex path). Returns 0 on failure. Calls FUN_000a2e3a() to set enc_type=WEP128, then FUN_000a2d32() to write 13-byte key to +0xf86. Single key only — WEP-128 firmware stores one key into all 4 hardware slots via CFG_Set_WEP128_Key_Slot.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_ui_process_wpa_key_input
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: WPA key input handler. If input is exactly 64 valid hex chars: hex-decodes to 32-byte PMK, calls FUN_000a2d51 (Tag 0x10). If input is 8-63 printable ASCII: copies raw passphrase, calls FUN_000a2d81 (Tag 0x12). Otherwise returns 0 (invalid). Note: Xbox never runs PBKDF2. Hex path sends pre-computed PMK. ASCII path sends plaintext. Stock firmware handles neither — Tag 0x10 is a stub, Tag 0x12 aborts the TLV parse loop.

FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Initializes the Ethernet receive buffer for incoming XPP frames. Calls KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel. Sets AutoClass1+0x14 = &DAT_copied_nlb_frame (the NLB copy buffer pointer). Clears _DAT_buffer_is_full_flag. Called at startup and after each received frame is consumed.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_calculate_handshake_hmac
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Calculates HMAC for HANDSHAKE_REQ/RESP validation. Inputs: cluster_ip (console IP) + source_mac (adapter MAC). Produces 20-byte HMAC-SHA1 digest; dashboard compares only the FIRST 16 bytes. Key derivation: console IP XOR'd with adapter MAC bytes. Called during HANDSHAKE_REQ construction and HANDSHAKE_RESP validation.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_fetch_adapter_wpa_caps
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Decodes WPA capability flags from two adapter capability bytes. param_1 points to the AutoClass1 object. Reads +0xba (byte174 caps) masked to 0x36, and +0xbb (byte175 caps) masked to 0x3f. Returns 1 if ALL of: +0xbb & 0x01 (WEP-64), +0xbb & 0x02 (WEP-128), +0xbb & 0x04 (Open) are set, AND NOT (+0xba & 0x20 set with +0xba & 0x10 clear). Returns 0 otherwise (adapter does not report full WPA capability). Used by xpp_select_best_security_mode to gate WPA option in the UI.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_select_best_security_mode
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: NOTE: Previously misnamed 'xpp_handle_handshake_response' in some sessions. Decodes capability bytes 174-175 from HANDSHAKE_RESP into a security mode integer. param_1 = byte174 (WPA/RSN caps): bit0x10=WPA1 present, bit0x20=WPA2 present. param_2 = byte175 (UI menu caps): bit0x04=WEP-128, bit0x02=WEP-64, bit0x01=Open. Reads AutoClass1+0xd70 (cap_wpa1_rsn, set from byte174 bit0x10). Priority: 4=WPA > 3=WEP-128 > 2=WEP-64 > 1=Open. Returns enc_type (1-4) stored at AutoClass1+0xe2e. Called from my_handle_nlb_handshake_response with payload bytes [0x116] and [0x117].

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_encode_tag09_link_state
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Encodes Tag 0x09 (link/network mode) value for CONNECT_REQ and ADAPTER_INFO_REQ. Reads AutoClass1+0xf5e (enc_type): returns 1 if enc=1, 2 if enc=2, 4 if enc=3, 0 otherwise. Maps internal enc type to XPP protocol link-state byte. Wire-verified: WEP-64 infrastructure = 0x02, WEP-128 infrastructure = 0x04.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_encode_tag08_auth_type
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Encodes Tag 0x08 (auth type/security mode) value for ADAPTER_INFO_REQ. param_1 = wep_flag (enc_type from +0xf5e), param_2 = net_mode (+0xf5c). wep_flag != 4 -> 0x00 (Open System auth) wep_flag == 4, net_mode != 0 -> 0x10 (Shared Key, infrastructure) wep_flag == 4, net_mode == 0 -> 0x20 (Shared Key, ad-hoc) Wire-verified across all capture logs.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_rssi_is_connected
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Returns true if adapter is in a connected state with valid RSSI. Checks: AutoClass1+0x0d == 0x01 (connected flag) AutoClass1+0x40 != 0x80000001 (not in error state) AutoClass1+0x48 > -0x48 (RSSI above -72 dBm minimum threshold) Used to gate RSSI-dependent UI display paths.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_rssi_alt_check
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Alternate RSSI validity check, used in scan/background polling context. Checks AutoClass1+0x5c == 0 AND AutoClass1+0x5d > -0x48 (-72 dBm). Returns true if the alternate (scan-phase) RSSI field is valid and above threshold.

FUNCTION.NAME: xpp_beacon_rssi_preprocess
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Pre-processes the RSSI byte pair from a BEACON_RESP before storing. param_1 = byte[0] (link_state), param_2 = byte[1] (raw RSSI). Likely implements RSSI smoothing/averaging. Return value discarded by caller. Called at top of xpp_handle_beacon_response before the link_state switch.

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_clear_connect_bitmask

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_copy_staged_to_cfg

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_set_admin_password

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_set_wep64_key_all_slots

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_set_wep128_key

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_set_wpa_pmk_raw

WPA PMK patch required to use this path. Previously misnamed AutoClass1_set_wep128_key in a prior Ghidra session.

FUNCTION.NAME: AutoClass1_set_wpa_passphrase
